name: Togo
tagline: Fifty kilometres wide, and a different country every hour north
summary: A narrow strip from the Atlantic to the Sahel: palm coast, the Kloto hills with the country's best walking, and the fortified Batammariba houses at Koutammakou that are a World Heritage site.
when: November to February. The south has a second dry spell in August.

entries.caption: Koutammakou
entries.description: The Batammariba build towered mud houses that are fortress, granary and shrine at once.
entries.subject: a Batammariba takienta tower house at Koutammakou

entries.caption: The Kloto Hills
entries.description: Coffee and cocoa country in the southwest, forested and cool, around Kpalime.
entries.subject: forested hills and a valley of cocoa near Kpalime

entries.caption: Fazao-Malfakassa
entries.description: Elephant, buffalo and a great many butterflies in the largest park in the country.
entries.subject: forest and grassland in Fazao-Malfakassa National Park

entries.caption: Small and Recovering
entries.description: The parks here are being rebuilt after decades of pressure, and the wildlife with them.
entries.subject: a waterhole and buffalo tracks in a Togolese reserve

entries.caption: Mont Agou
entries.description: 986 metres, the highest point, walkable in a morning from Kpalime.
entries.subject: the forested cone of Mont Agou above villages and farms

entries.caption: Kpime and Womé
entries.description: Two falls in the Kloto hills, both of them a short walk off the Kpalime road.
entries.subject: the Womé waterfall falling into a pool in forest near Kpalime

entries.caption: Lake Togo and the Mono
entries.description: A shallow lagoon behind the coast, and the Mono river marking the Benin border.
entries.subject: pirogues on the shallow water of Lake Togo

entries.caption: Fifty Kilometres of Coast
entries.description: Palm-backed Atlantic sand from Lome east to Aneho, with a heavy swell.
entries.subject: coconut palms and Atlantic surf on the beach near Aneho

entries.caption: The Kloto Forest
entries.description: Semi-deciduous forest above Kpalime, and one of the richest butterfly sites in West Africa.
entries.subject: butterflies on a forest path in the Kloto hills

entries.caption: Walking Around Kpalime
entries.description: Waterfalls, coffee farms, Mont Agou and the butterfly forest, all within an hour.
entries.subject: a walking path through cocoa and coffee smallholdings near Kpalime

entries.caption: Ewe, Kabye, Tem, Batammariba
entries.description: Ewe in the south, Kabye in the centre, Batammariba in the far northwest.
entries.subject: an Ewe drumming group performing in a village

entries.caption: The Batammariba
entries.description: Their name means 'those who shape the earth', and the houses are the argument.
entries.subject: a Batammariba woman on the roof terrace of a takienta house

entries.caption: Fufu and Gboma Dessi
entries.description: Fufu with groundnut sauce, and gboma dessi — spinach stew with fish.
entries.subject: a bowl of gboma dessi spinach stew with fufu

entries.caption: Evala and the Voodoo Market
entries.description: Kabye wrestling in July, and the Akodessewa fetish market in Lome all year.
entries.subject: young men wrestling at the Evala festival in Kabye country

entries.caption: Batik and Pottery
entries.description: Batik and wood carving around Kpalime, and pottery from the north.
entries.subject: batik cloth drying on a line at a Kpalime workshop

entries.caption: Aneho and the Old Coast
entries.description: The first colonial capital, with German and Afro-Brazilian buildings going quietly to seed.
entries.subject: a decaying German colonial building in Aneho

entries.caption: Koutammakou, Listed
entries.description: The Batammariba landscape has been a World Heritage site since 2004, and is still lived in.
entries.subject: a cluster of takienta tower houses among fields at Koutammakou

entries.caption: Lome
entries.description: The only capital on a border, with the biggest market in the region behind the beach.
entries.subject: the beach and palm-lined boulevard at Lome

entries.caption: Towers of Mud
entries.description: Takienta houses with granaries on top, and German colonial stone in Lome and Aneho.
entries.subject: the sculpted mud tower and granary of a takienta house

entries.caption: The Grand Marche and the Nana Benz
entries.description: The women who built the wax-print trade ran it from this market, and still do.
entries.subject: wax print cloth stacked at a stall in Lome's Grand Marche

entries.caption: Beach and Waterfall in a Day
entries.description: Togo is narrow enough that the coast and the Kloto hills are the same short trip.
entries.subject: a family swimming in a pool below a waterfall near Kpalime

entries.caption: Mont Agou at Dawn
entries.description: Up before six, and Ghana visible across the valley by seven.
entries.subject: the view from Mont Agou across valleys at first light

entries.caption: A Handful
entries.description: Beach hotels at Lome and a few good places at Kpalime.
entries.subject: a beach hotel terrace under palms near Lome

entries.caption: Butterflies at Kloto
entries.description: Over five hundred species recorded in one forest, and a local guiding tradition around them.
entries.subject: a guide showing butterflies in the Kloto forest

entries.caption: Earth Architecture
entries.description: Koutammakou late in the day, when the mud goes gold and the granaries throw shadows.
entries.subject: late sun on the sculpted walls of takienta houses

entries.caption: Aneho and Lake Togo
entries.description: An hour east of Lome: a lagoon, a decayed colonial town, and no visitors.
entries.subject: a quiet street of faded colonial houses at Aneho

entries.caption: Why Togo
entries.description: A whole cross-section of West Africa in a country you can drive in a day.
entries.subject: a road running north through changing country in Togo
